Requires: https://github.com/mono/skia/pull/367
Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/pull/5081
Changes: https://github.com/google/skia/compare/9f9e6beb751091ef69163d2b4fdcd1e711b594ac...2466dcf3937437e217e7f284afe0e1aae15891ce

Keep the final Chrome M154 Ganesh correction on release/4.154.x and pin the
SkiaSharp metadata to the exact native merge.

The m154 release branches were cut from the corresponding main and skiasharp
tips before the pending m155 update. Target this change to release/4.154.x so
the buffer-upload correction remains available to the m154 servicing line
without coupling it to main's milestone transition.

2b5a672d1a5eede30a22e4c9dc883ffb99d9f745

That merge contains the reviewed native commit and has the identical tree.

~~ Reject stale GPU buffer data ~~

Under high memory pressure, GrGpuBuffer::updateData() can fail while staging
data for a draw. Several native callers previously ignored that result and
continued as though the GPU buffer contained current data, which could allow
stale buffer contents to be drawn.

The native update propagates failures through buffer allocation and pre-draw
setup, rejects incomplete static and GL helper buffers, and drops affected
draws. Triangulated paths retain CPU-backed vertex data so a later draw can
retry GPU-buffer creation.

The upstream range changes no C API or DEPS state. Independent regeneration
matches all five maintained binding outputs, so package versions, native ABI,
and the managed API remain unchanged.

5111.title: Fix BinSkim BA2007 for libHarfBuzzSharp by scoping C4244/C4267 suppression
5111.body:
libHarfBuzzSharp.dll fails BinSkim rule BA2007 (EnableCriticalCompilerWarnings)
at error severity, because libHarfBuzzSharp.vcxproj passed
<DisableSpecificWarnings>4267;4244</DisableSpecificWarnings> in all six
ItemDefinitionGroups. C4244 and C4267 are the "possible loss of data" truncation
warnings BinSkim policy does not allow to be suppressed, so the /wd4244 /wd4267
recorded in the PDB failed the rule.

This breaks consumers, not just us: Microsoft-internal CI runs BinSkim in break
mode, and anything that takes SkiaSharp picks up HarfBuzzSharp.NativeAssets.Win32
transitively (Svg.Skia 5.x does), then fails its security gate on a binary it
does not build. The only workaround available today is to baseline it.

The project compiles exactly one translation unit -- the vendored
harfbuzz-subset.cc, itself an amalgamation of 73 upstream HarfBuzz sources -- so
there is no other object file to scope the suppression to, and BinSkim names
harfbuzz-subset.obj precisely because it is the whole binary. Building with the
suppressions removed produces 1196 warnings (976 C4244, 220 C4267), every one of
them inside vendored HarfBuzz headers and sources, so simply dropping them is not
viable and patching upstream code is not desirable.

Instead, add a small SkiaSharp-owned translation unit that wraps the vendored
amalgamation in #pragma warning(push/disable/pop) and compile that. The
suppression now lives in source rather than on the command line, so the compiler
command line recorded in the PDB is free of disabled warnings and BA2007 passes,
while any first-party code added to this project in future still gets the
warnings. libSkiaSharp is untouched -- it is clang-built and already passes.

Verified on Windows with BinSkim 4.4.9.11 (the version in the report):

  before  BA2007 error  Error_WarningsDisabled ... [Explicitly disabled warnings: 4244;4267]
  after   BA2007 pass

BA2007 now reports kind=pass on x64, ARM64 and Win32, and those are the only
results that changed -- the pre-existing BA2024/BA2025/BA2026/BA2027 warnings are
unaffected. All three platforms build with 0 warnings and 0 errors, the DLL still
exports the same 560 symbols (no ABI change), and the rebuilt binary loads and
shapes correctly (hb_version_string reports 14.2.1).

Fixes #5108

5034.title: [release] Coordinate release state and finalization
5034.body:
[release] Coordinate release state and finalization (#5034)

Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/actions/runs/35276546957
Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/actions/runs/35276546972
Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/actions/runs/35276547027
Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/actions/runs/35276547081

Make release progress recoverable from repository and service evidence rather
than requiring maintainers to infer which phase-specific tool to run. Add one
line audit for start, build, publication, synchronization, and Finish work, and
make Finish carry its shipment through milestone maintenance. The audit reads
remote services and fetches local Git objects without changing release state.

~~ Choose the next release transition ~~

Release work can overlap across `main`, servicing branches, specific release
branches, exact NuGet shipments, tags, and GitHub Releases. Add
`audit-release-state.ps1 -Version A.B` to correlate those surfaces and emit
ordered Finish, publication, synchronization, build, and Prepare actions.

Compare maintenance with the latest cut using patch equivalence rather than raw
ancestry. Ignore at most one automatic version bump when its subject and exact
two-file change match the repository convention. Preserve superseded branches
without suggesting that immutable package versions be republished.

Before a new cut, compare the exact `chrome/mN` head with the existing
mono/skia sync branch, falling back to the line's mono/skia base. Keep
`skia-sync/main` separate from milestone syncs, report parent/native gitlink
mismatches as inconsistent, and recognize the immediately following milestone
while its `skia-sync/mN` PR is still targeting `main`.

Emit an aligned human table and structured JSON. Redirected output has no
interactive decoration. Exit 0 means no action, exit 1 means work or an
inconsistency remains, and exit 2 means a required check was unavailable.

~~ Require exact build evidence ~~

Add `AzureDevOps.Common.psm1` to query internal `skiasharp-package` definition
1642 for the maintenance tip and latest unpublished branch, then select the
highest-ID build whose `sourceVersion` equals that exact branch-tip SHA.

Require a completed successful build with one `BAR ID - N` tag before
recommending Prepare or publication. Preserve running, failed, canceled,
missing, BAR-less, and unavailable results; unavailable build evidence keeps
the other findings but forces exit 2.

Add a compact `release-audit` skill for range expansion, aggregation, exception
investigation, and confirmed handoffs. Deterministic release and build
classification remains in tested PowerShell.

~~ Read remote refs without shared fetch state ~~

Advertised branch SHAs were not necessarily available locally, recursive fetch
could fail on a missing Skia gitlink, and repository-global `FETCH_HEAD` let
parallel audits consume another process's fetch result.

Fetch advertised parent commits directly with `--no-recurse-submodules` and
`--no-tags`, then resolve immutable SHAs instead of `FETCH_HEAD`. Use
pattern-scoped branch and tag maps, a tag-keyed Release map, and exact head/base
PR queries. Treat stale parent sync gitlinks and mono/skia-only sync branches as
inconsistent until the parent side carries the expected native commit.

~~ Bootstrap Skia sync before workload installation ~~

The four Context runs were sibling manual dispatches of one workflow revision.
Each passed pre-activation and apt setup, then failed before agent execution
because `dotnet workload install android` ran without the SDK 10.0.401 required
by `global.json`, producing exit code 155.

Use `./eng/common/dotnet.sh workload install android --skip-sign-check` so the
repository bootstrap installs the pinned SDK first. Regenerate the compiled
workflow and add a regression test that rejects a bare Android workload
invocation.

~~ Serialize Finish through milestone maintenance ~~

Finish previously published the tag and GitHub Release while assignment
reconciliation and milestone rollover remained a separate manual operation.
Make `Release - Milestones` reusable and require it after Finish for preview,
RC, stable, patch, and four-part hotfix shipments. Reconcile shipped PR and
linked-issue ownership before updating dates, rolling open work forward, and
closing shipped milestones. Retain standalone dispatch controls for repairs.

Export the resolved public version, numeric release, tag, and NuGet source
commit. When the tag is absent, dry runs use that pair as a virtual shipment so
milestone plans model the post-tag state. Push runs re-read and require the
remote tag at the same commit before milestone writes. Reject packages whose
nuspec branch differs from the release identity or whose source commit is not
reachable from that branch.

Hold the global `release-state` lock through Finish and milestone completion.
Standalone repairs share the lock, while the nested reusable call uses a
run-specific child group so it cannot deadlock its caller.

~~ Keep merge history relative to the PR base ~~

Merge-message drafting could treat an intra-PR refactor as repository history,
producing `move`, `replace`, or `extract` claims whose source never existed at
the PR base. Require those change verbs to be proven against the base and
describe branch-local refactors as final net additions instead. Add an
evaluation covering a skill and module that are both introduced by one PR.

Current-head tooling tests passed 261 publishing assertions, 60 milestone
assertions, and 5 workflow-safety tests.

5054.title: [skia-sync] Merge upstream Chrome M154 bug fixes
5054.body:
[skia-sync] Merge upstream Chrome M154 bug fixes (#5054)

Requires: https://github.com/mono/skia/pull/359
Changes: https://github.com/google/skia/compare/7b950f0d8ed1028a75248ea69813ae6054ca65f8...9f9e6beb751091ef69163d2b4fdcd1e711b594ac

Advance the Skia submodule to the reviewed and merged mono/skia commit
9af1dc69083843cb11faf236fab8eb6ec6742e20. This is a same-milestone M154
bug-fix sync, so package, assembly, file, and native ABI versions remain
unchanged.

~~ Glyph-atlas generation tracking ~~

Prevent Ganesh and Graphite text rendering from recording a current atlas
generation after only a partial glyph-vector update. Earlier glyphs may have
been evicted while a subrun was split across flushes, making the generation
fast path reuse stale atlas locations.

Reset the bulk-use updater when the atlas generation changes and record the
generation only when one successful pass starts at glyph zero and covers the
complete vector.

~~ Ganesh failure propagation ~~

Separate render-task and flush success from semaphore submission. Propagate
task execution failures through GrDrawingManager and GrDirectContext, stop
image factories and backend-handle extraction after failed prerequisite
flushes, and complete unsupported asynchronous readbacks with a null callback
result.

The existing C flush exports remain ABI-compatible void operations. Existing
false, null, and invalid-result contracts represent the newly propagated
native failures, so no C API, managed API, or generated binding change is
required.

The review preserved 91 non-interop fork patches, 108 interop patches, and 19
dependency entries unchanged. Independent generation matched all five binding
directories, and the final mono/skia merge tree is identical to the reviewed
native tree.

5027.title: [release] Keep milestones with their first shipped release
5027.body:
[release] Keep milestones with their first shipped release (#5027)

Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/actions/runs/33984759273
Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/actions/runs/34065404228
Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/pull/4694

Assign shipped pull requests and linked issues to the lowest semantic release
that contains their fix. Derive ownership from immutable tags and the complete
Git DAG so parallel release branches remain independent of publication and
workflow execution order.

~~ Tag-derived release ownership ~~

The 4.154 reconciliation used `v4.151.2` as its previous boundary because the
algorithm considered only stable releases and 4.152 and 4.153 had shipped only
prerelease tags. Its first-parent range consequently included 31 PRs already
shipped in `4.153.0-preview.1` together with the m154 Skia update, and moved all
32 items into `4.154.0-preview.1`.

Discover every shipped identity from exact release tags. For each tag, inspect
the complete reachable DAG and subtract commits reachable from every
semantically earlier tag. Union multiple exact tags for one identity, recognize
both squash and merge commit subjects, and retain the first semantic owner when
a PR is relanded in a later preview, stable, hotfix, or parallel release line.

Parse preview and RC iterations numerically; tests explicitly establish
`preview.2 < preview.10 < stable`. Keep merge-base and first-parent topology for
boundary diagnostics rather than membership. Unshipped previews still roll
forward to the next shipped preview, RC, or stable milestone.

Read-only reconciliation at the final head found:

  * 4.152.0: 19 assignments to `4.152.0-rc.1`, with 71 already
    correct.
  * 4.153.0: 31 assignments from `4.154.0-preview.1` back to
    `4.153.0-preview.1`.
  * 4.154.0: no assignments, with the m154 Skia update #4945 already
    correct.

~~ Repository-scoped linked issues ~~

GitHub closing references include their repository, but reconciliation retained
only the issue number. PR #4694 closes
`appium/appium-mac2-driver#410`; dropping that repository identity caused the
unrelated `mono/SkiaSharp#410` issue to receive a SkiaSharp release milestone.

Retain `repository.nameWithOwner`, paginate closing-reference queries, and
ignore references outside `mono/SkiaSharp`. When multiple shipped local PRs
close one issue, assign that issue to the lowest semantic owner among all of
those PRs rather than whichever release reconciliation runs first.

~~ Mutation safety and repair ~~

Block plans that would move an item out of an earlier closed or shipped
milestone. Refresh tags and recompute complete PR or linked-issue ownership
before and after each PATCH. If a concurrent shipment invalidates ownership
after mutation, restore the observed source milestone, including no milestone,
unless another actor has already changed the item.

The publishing suites pass 113 tests and the focused milestone suite passes 56
tests, including full-DAG membership, deleted release branches, duplicate tags,
parallel lines, cross-repository references, multiple closing PRs, ownership
races, and restoration to a milestone or no milestone.

After this change reaches `main`, the existing assignments can be repaired by
rerunning **Release - Milestones**. The workflow accepts one numeric version per
dispatch, so run 4.152.0 and 4.153.0 separately; their order no longer affects
ownership.

First run each version with both operations selected and `push` disabled. After
reviewing the plans, apply assignment-only repairs with `reconcile=true`,
`update=false`, and `push=true`. Leave `update=true` only when the displayed
date, roll-forward, and closure plan is also intended. Run 4.154.0 read-only to
confirm convergence.

The corrected workflow will not clear unrelated `mono/SkiaSharp#410`, because
it no longer treats the foreign closing reference as local. Remove that
historically incorrect milestone separately after merge.

5015.title: [skia-sync] Streamline evidence-driven updates
5015.body:
Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/pull/4991
Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/actions/runs/33936493725
Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/actions/runs/33983819134

Reduce repeated model work and avoid known false starts in the Skia update
playbook while retaining independent review, source-build, binding, and
unfiltered test gates. Keep deterministic helpers responsible for version and
dependency facts, and let long Copilot sessions continue across natural prompt
boundaries instead of moving validation into post-steps.

~~ Python 3.9 compatibility ~~

A live run resolved bare `python3` to PyPy 3.9. Evaluated PEP 604 annotations
failed before `update_versions.py` could run, and the agent had to probe
installed interpreters before retrying with Python 3.12.

Postpone annotations in both helpers and replace the Python-3.10-only
`Path.write_text(newline=...)` calls with `Path.open`. This supports the Python
3.9 runner environment without adding a runtime probe.

~~ Pre-build milestone drift detection ~~

An upstream-main run retained managed milestone 154 while target source had
already advanced `SK_MILESTONE` to 155. The mismatch reached Cake, where native
setup failed before compilation and required a second build after an explicit
fork adaptation.

Make `update_versions.py` validate `SkMilestone.h` before changing metadata.
A mismatch now stops at the version gate and asks for a committed,
evidence-backed fork adaptation. The regression test proves this failure
leaves version and manifest files unchanged.

~~ Independent validator provenance ~~

Phase 03 produced an independent review, but later phase guidance told the
parent to replace its disposition after new build evidence appeared. The final
artifact therefore mixed validator findings with parent-authored conclusions.

Save the validator response verbatim and integrate its discrepancies into the
primary analysis. Later parent findings may use a separate optional follow-up;
they never rewrite or become a required delivery artifact. The shorter
validator prompt pins checks to exact SHAs and covers changed sources, headers,
modules, build lists, C API behavior, GPU families, struct layouts, and
fork-relative dependency decisions.

~~ One canonical full test run ~~

The earlier successful workflow executed two unchanged green full suites, with
identical host totals. The second run existed only because the playbook required
separate initial and final artifacts.

Run the unfiltered solution directly once, capture its normal output and exit
code, and treat that green result as final while semantic and native content
remain unchanged. Preserve a failed attempt before focused diagnostics and
rerun the same command only after an actual fix. Do not add a result parser,
fingerprint layer, or stricter post-agent gate.

~~ Phase guidance consolidation ~~

The evidence runs searched for nonexistent phase files, reread unchanged
phases, and printed broad dependency, status, and validator output into model
context. Other references also said both to keep dependency pins and to
classify them, and implied cleanly merged patches escaped the complete fork
audit.

Route through each exact linked phase once, keep broad inventories in artifact
files, state the ancestry check direction, and remove duplicated testing and
conflicting merge guidance. Retain the evidence-based dependency, complete
fork-delta, native source-build, managed wrapper, GPU, and final delivery
gates.

~~ Long-running Copilot completion ~~

Two proof runs reached Copilot prompt completion near the 30-minute boundary
with a managed-build or test shell call still pending, so the agent exited
successfully before Phase 10 and Phase 11 completed. Pinning Copilot CLI 1.0.83
did not change that behavior.

Enable three Copilot autopilot continuations, the gh-aw mechanism for incomplete
long-running tasks. Run 33988240432 then completed the cold Linux x64 source

and AI credits from 524.99 to 374.41.

passed. Python and shell syntax checks, diff validation, and gh-aw v0.88.2
strict compilation of all six workflows also passed with zero warnings.

4974.body:
[samples] Update WASM smoke harnesses to Playwright 1.55.1 (#4974)

Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/actions/runs/33921909157
Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/actions/runs/33926338035
Changes: https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/compare/v1.49.0...v1.55.1

Update the Gallery Uno and SkiaFiddle smoke harnesses together so their shared
browser cache cannot leave either harness with a Playwright and Chromium
version mismatch.

~~ Playwright and Chromium update ~~

Move both exact `playwright` dependencies from 1.49.0 to 1.55.1. This advances
bundled Chromium from 131.0.6778.33 revision 1148 to 140.0.7339.186 revision
1193. Both Playwright versions require Node.js 18 or newer, so the runtime
minimum remains unchanged.

Playwright 1.55 drops Chromium Manifest V2 extension support, but these drivers
launch bundled headless Chromium without extensions and require no API changes.

~~ Version-aligned smoke setup ~~

The scripts previously ran `npm install` only when `node_modules/playwright`
was absent and accepted any `chromium-*` cache directory as sufficient. Since
both harnesses use `$HOME/.cache/ms-playwright`, running them with different
Playwright versions could make the second harness skip its required browser
download. The mixed-version workflow failed when Playwright 1.49 requested
`chromium_headless_shell-1148` after only the 1.55 browser had been installed.

Run `npm install` and `playwright install chromium` for each harness invocation.
This delegates package and browser reconciliation to npm and Playwright's exact
revision metadata instead of directory-existence checks.

The combined Pages - Deploy run completed both the Gallery Uno and SkiaFiddle
WASM smoke tests successfully.
